method: Consult existing problem-category and donor decisions, compare named atoms serially, seal exact per-file preimages/postimages, qualify actual OpenRewrite SDK Results, then admit all target inputs before serial receiving.
invariant: Maintain reusable validated transformation recipes; use contract-preserving per-file transformations; record category-driven donor comparison and selection rationale. A source fingerprint is candidate evidence, never semantic-equivalence or mutation authority.

operations.before: The nullable neighbor result was treated as stored null only when null was the first or last owner element. A lawful comparator can place null between two stored nonnull elements.
operations.selected: Adapt the previously reviewed actual-stored-boundary proof. Retain current first/last acquisition order and compare the stored opposite extreme when neither extreme is null.

rejected.candidate: contains(null) or fabricated null comparator probe
rejected.reason: Adds a potentially illegal probe and observable callbacks for a nonnull owner; historical catalogue already retains this counterexample.

rejected.candidate: Full owner scan or sorted snapshot
rejected.reason: Changes demand, callback/exception order and live owner semantics; unnecessary for the selected presence atom.

operations.scope: Existing read-only NavigableSetView neighbor queries, including legal bounded and descending owners; no change to comparator ownership or range creation.
operations.observable_change: When both stored extremes are nonnull, the repaired null-sentinel branch performs one comparison with the actual opposite stored boundary where the baseline short-circuited. Current first/last lookup order and finite comparator/value results are established; universal comparator callback identity is not claimed. This repaired path is excluded from the unchanged ordinary-read tape.

operations.before: Abstract entry-set membership compared detached entry keys with equals, inconsistent with the backing sorted map's comparator equivalence and stored representative predicate contract.
operations.selected: Use existing storedKey/get atoms following the pinned Synexia stored-entry donor. Evaluate visibility on the actual stored key; compare the actual value to candidate entry value.

rejected.reason: Fails comparator-equivalent keys with different equality/identity and can hide or reveal the wrong stored entry.

rejected.candidate: Entry allocation from the historical donor
rejected.reason: Current source already provides the required storedKey/get atoms; no detached Entry is needed.

operations.observable_change: Corrected entrySet.contains calls its predicate once on a stored comparator-matching key, avoids unrelated predicates and reads candidate value once. This repaired path is excluded from unchanged callback-tape claims.

operations.before: Inherited JDK21 sequenced removal on empty views and reversed sorted range defaults could throw NoSuchElementException or permit no-op mutation instead of the documented unconditional UnsupportedOperationException.
operations.selected: Reuse pinned explicit endpoint refusals and query-forwarding ReadOnlySortedSet guard.

rejected.reason: Does not establish the required empty sequenced endpoint behavior throughout reversed/range wrappers.
Invokes owner reads or predicate callbacks before a required unconditional refusal.

operations.scope: No public callable descriptor is added; inherited public descriptors can acquire explicit declaring-owner reflection metadata.
operations.unreconciled_historical_map_guarantee: PR#1204 README m3/collections/qualification/contracts-20261017/README.md (blob9d1e977abaceade36e51df6b0179e3b5db6540a3) promised strict empty sequenced endpoints for read-only maps and sorted sets. This candidate refines only Set guards. Current outer JDK-derived Map wrappers can still inherit NoSuchElementException on empty derived endpoints. That historical guarantee remains unreconciled, requiring separate admission of concrete wrapper/marker/delegation behavior.

operations.before: Repeated known CollectionView/SetView wrappers recurse through iterator and membership, overflowing the Java stack at tested depths.
operations.selected: Reuse pinned iterationView, membershipView and visibleMember continuation atoms without changing source links.

rejected.candidate: Flatten predicate chains when constructing wrappers
rejected.reason: Alters repeated inner scans and callback occurrence/order needed by the existing membership contract.

rejected.candidate: Unwrap arbitrary sorted, navigable or foreign views
rejected.reason: Their membership and callback boundaries are opaque.

operations.cost: Iterator uses O(d) temporary predicate references and constant M3 stack; per-element predicate demand remains O(d). Contains retains repeated scans, including d(d+1)/2 predicates for one always-visible element. No linear-time membership claim.
operations.scope: Known generic collection and exact SetView chains only; temporary arrays contain references to behavioral state, not element snapshots.

operations.before: scanWindow's source/output guard omitted requiredMasks and forbiddenMasks. Java wrote into those inputs and could subsequently throw ConcurrentModificationException; actual JNI could return successfully after corrupting those masks.
operations.selected: Add both mask arrays to the existing output/input reference-identity guard, before backend selection and before any writes.

rejected.reason: Adds allocation and silently permits input/output aliases despite the existing documented alias-preflight rule.
Misses JAVA behavior and changes the wrong owner; common Java admission precedes both backends.

operations.cost: Two extra constant-time identity comparisons; existing bounded two-pass selection, duplicate row order, signed stride, offset mapping and cursor packing unchanged.
operations.scope: All output/input aliases refuse including empty paths and zero limits. Input/input sharing remains permitted when separately valid. Existing geometry/output-bounds failure priority remains.

discovery_reference_only.use: Selected first-party Apache-2.0 continuation and guard atoms; exact commit/blob in DONOR_SOURCES.tsv.
Sorted-boundary problem category and adversarial duplicate/boundary shapes; no submission or editorial source copied.
Stable compaction problem category; confirms encounter-order obligation differs from in-place remove-element challenges. No algorithm change selected for current compaction owner.
State-bit operation category; existing M3 required/forbidden-mask implementation retained. No challenge source copied.
Stable ordering category. Snapshot sorting/permutation replacement rejected for live wrappers; no challenge source copied.
Lower-bound comparison category only; no article code transplanted.
Stable ordering classification only; no article code transplanted.
Sequenced/sorted public API behavioral reference and independent JDK owner oracle; no GPL source copied.

rights: Existing M3 and Synexia Apache-2.0 source headers and module licenses are retained. Only pinned first-party atoms are reused. Challenge platforms, Guava and JDK are reference-only for this maintenance pass.

verification.authoring: Raw baseline failures, candidate checks and stable unaffected-read tape are frozen under AUTHORING_WITNESSES; authoring is distinct from receiving.
verification.recipe: Unchanged canonical OpenRewrite 8.17.1 Java/Text owners; existing five SDK tests, eight prepare tests and nine receiver cases must pass. No replacement harness.
verification.receiving: Use receive.py --check after SDK qualification, then receive actual retained SDK outputs. Runtime checks must run against received sources.
verification.status_resolution: Frozen authoring records do not predict later execution. See ../../evidence/filtered-navigation-20261018/ for exact SDK, receiver and runtime status receipts.
verification.tape_scope: Unchanged ordinary-read tape excludes both repaired entry-membership demand and repaired null-sentinel comparator demand; neither correction is represented as universal baseline callback equivalence.
